questions.prompt: A frozen shallow preview shares draft.stats. Which statement is correct?

options.label: The binding is fixed; the nested object remains shared and mutable.
Every nested value becomes immutable because the outer binding uses const.
The spread copy necessarily duplicates the complete object graph.

questions.explanation: const restricts reassignment and the outer freeze restricts its own descriptors. Neither recursively copies or freezes draft.stats. A changed nested field is observed through both references; the two outer objects remain distinct.

questions.prompt: An item is absent and indexOf returns -1. How should a delete helper act?

options.label: Check for -1 before splice; the missing item must leave the list unchanged.
Pass -1 to splice to express that no item was found.
Clear the list to avoid leaving an unrecognized item behind.

questions.explanation: A negative splice start addresses from the end, so passing -1 removes the last element. Check the search result before mutation. Clearing the collection changes unrelated state and violates the absent-target contract.

questions.prompt: An object inherits a name and has enumerable, hidden and symbol properties. What does Object.keys expose?

options.label: Object.keys lists enumerable own string keys; inherited keys are separate.
Object.keys lists every field that ordinary property lookup can find.
Object.keys recursively lists symbol keys and all hidden properties.

questions.explanation: Object.keys includes only enumerable own string keys. Inherited lookup can succeed without ownership; non-enumerable and symbol keys require different inspection. None of these enumeration APIs recursively flattens nested values.

questions.prompt: A cheat sheet says 5 == true. What does the selected equality rule predict?

options.label: 5 == true is false; true converts to 1, which differs from 5.
It is true because every nonzero number is loosely equal to true.
It is true because strict equality first converts both operands to strings.

questions.explanation: Loose equality converts the boolean to a number for this comparison, giving 5 versus 1. Truthiness is a different operation. Strict equality does not apply that coercion, so converting both values to strings is not its rule.

questions.prompt: An ordinary method is called on another object, while an arrow was captured inside origin.capture. What differs?

options.label: The ordinary function uses its call receiver; the captured arrow retains its lexical this.
Both always use the object where their source text was written.
call can replace the captured arrow receiver just as it replaces an ordinary receiver.

questions.explanation: The ordinary function gets its receiver from the invocation; a strict detached call may have undefined this. The captured arrow keeps the enclosing this and call cannot replace it. Source location alone does not bind ordinary methods.
